neboas-card: A narrative game about a witch with a clandestine potion shop
neboas-intro: Neboa's Hut is a casual, crafting video game with a strong focus on narrative and dialogue. You play as a witch trying to manage a clandestine potion shop, this means talking with customers, gathering ingredients, and preparing the potions to be sold.
neboas-intro2: The gameplay revolves around earning enough money to pay the taxes that are periodically demanded and trying no to raise too much suspicion so that the Inquisition doesn't discover you. Therefore, depending on the situation, the player must decide whether to sell an effective remedy or try to remain undetected.
neboas-role: This project was carried out in collaboration with other members of Conxuro Studio; my roles fell within the areas of design and technical development in Unreal Engine, including:
neboas-role-en1: Management of the design department as lead and the workflow within it.
neboas-role-en2: Core gameplay design and potion system.
neboas-role-en4: Controls and player movement system programming.
neboas-role-en7: Tecnical art - optimizations, materials, and VFX.
neboas-design1: Neboa's Hut was designed with player accessibility in mind; its core design fosters a calm gameplay experience, free from complex mechanics. I chose to lean into this aspect when developing the game's other systems. For instance, the entire experience can be enjoyed using only the mouse cursor, allowing even less experienced players to engage with the game without needing to memorize key bindings. That said, keyboard shortcuts and alternative control schemes were also included, giving players the freedom to choose how they wish to experience the game.
neboas-design2: When designing the potion system, I took the game's genre very much into account. Although it functions internally using a system of numerical values, it is presented to the player in a narrative way, through descriptions found within the protagonist's book.
neboas-design3: Furthermore, I wanted to move away from any system based on predefined recipes, giving the player the freedom to experiment and discover various ways to create the same potion.
neboas-design4: To further enhance player immersion, I decided to incorporate interactive minigames to be performed during the potion-making process, such as lighting the fire or crushing ingredients inside a mortar. In keeping with the established accessibility criteria, these minigames were designed as interactive experiences with no actual difficulty or time limits.
neboas-design5: The in-game menu includes both standard video game menu options and the descriptions for potions, ingredients, and village residents. To ensure easy access, I have organized the content into separate sections, each accessible individually and featuring its own internal index. You can also navigate by flipping through the pages one by one, which connects the various description sections.
neboas-design6: The elements were organized so that those requiring more frequent access would involve less navigation and be easier to find. To represent the design, I created a flowchart of all the content.
neboas-curve1: The biggest technical challenge I encountered was getting the menu elements to conform to the curvature of the book image used as a background, since Unreal Engine does not natively include a tool for deforming widgets as desired.
neboas-curve2: To solve this problem, I created a post-processing material that modifies the vertical position of elements located above the book based on their vertical coordinate. To easily adjust this effect, the amount of displacement is determined by a curve asset.
neboas-curve3: The only drawback of this approach is that the collision boundaries of interactive elements do not get their positions updated. To address this, I used custom buttons that trigger a function to reverse the transformations applied to the element's visual representation. This allows the position of the collision boundary to be modified while keeping its visual representation fixed on the canvas.
neboas-opt1: Due to the high graphical cost of Unreal Engine 5, I implemented several optimizations to improve the project's performance. I opted to forgo systems like Lumen and Nanite, replacing them with less demanding alternatives such as static lighting, screen-space reflections, and traditional LODs. I also limited the number of lights per room, simplified geometries, and optimized materials using material instances—thereby reducing draw calls and employing low-complexity shaders. Furthermore, I adjusted texture resolutions based on their size on screen, which resulted in a 50% reduction in memory usage.
neboas-opt2: Additionally, I implemented level streaming to load only the necessary rooms and their adjacent areas, avoiding unnecessary resource consumption and jarring visual transitions. I also developed solutions for managing object references and behavior during level unloading. Finally, I simplified collisions by using basic geometric shapes and removed those not required for gameplay, thereby improving the project's overall performance.
